text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provides(x, y, z) ::: x provides y to z.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to take y.
GRE(x) ::: x is the GRE test.
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is financial aid.
Tom(x) ::: x is Tom.
Something(x) ::: x is something.
Conclusion:
Cost(gre, 205) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (GRE(x) → (ETS → ∀y (Provides(ETS, FinancialAid(y), x)))) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
(SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x)) → Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(tom) ∧ FewResources(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family. Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
Applying(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
¬∃x (Applying(x, gre) ∧ ∃y (Provides(y, FinancialAid(z), x))) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
